label: Daniel (founder & engineer)
tagline: Seven years from first job to startup exit track: building, fundraising, and learning to rest.

entries.title: First engineering job
entries.body: Started as a junior backend engineer. Everything is on fire and I love it. Goal: ship something real in my first quarter.

entries.title: Picked up Go
entries.body: Rewrote our log pipeline in Go over two weekends. Concurrency finally clicks: channels are just queues with good manners.

entries.title: Sam Ortiz — first manager
entries.body: Sam Ortiz manages the platform team. Direct, generous with context, allergic to status theater. I want his one-pager habit.

entries.title: Remote, suddenly
entries.body: Office closed mid-sprint. Kitchen-table desk, standups on video. Output held; serendipity died. Started a Friday demo ritual to compensate.

entries.title: Back pain audit
entries.body: Six months of couch-coding: lower back complains daily. Standing desk, hourly walks, and a hard stop at six. Non-negotiable now.

entries.title: Incidents teach more than launches
entries.body: Three outages this year wrote our real architecture doc. Blameless write-ups, one fix per incident, no heroics. Reliability is a writing practice.

entries.title: Side project: deploy previews
entries.body: Built preview deploys for side projects. Two friends asked to pay. That sentence rewired my year: maybe this is a company.

entries.title: June Park — co-founder?
entries.body: June Park, product designer from the meetup circuit. We whiteboarded the preview-deploy idea for three hours and left with a company name. Testing the partnership with a 4-week build sprint.

entries.title: Quit-or-commit deadline
entries.body: Giving the side project until March: ten paying teams or back to full-time focus. Savings cover seven months. Written down so I can't move the goalposts.

entries.title: Runway spreadsheet v1
entries.body: Personal runway: 7 months at current burn. Business costs near zero until incorporation. Every expense now asks: does this buy learning or comfort?

entries.title: Incorporated today
entries.body: Filed the Delaware C-corp, opened the business account, cried a little at the kitchen table. We have ten paying teams. It's real now.

entries.title: Weekly founder notes
entries.body: Friday note, three sections: what shipped, what I learned, what I'm avoiding. Shared with June unedited. Avoidance is the section that matters.

entries.title: Alex Kim — first hire
entries.body: Alex Kim joins as founding engineer in January. Brilliant systems thinker, calmer than me under incident pressure. Equity and salary both written down, no handshake math.

entries.title: Onboarding beats features
entries.body: Churn interviews said the same thing twelve ways: teams didn't fail to love the product, they failed to reach first value. We rebuilt onboarding; activation doubled.

entries.title: First investor update
entries.body: Monthly update format locked: metrics, one win, one miss, one ask. Investors reply to asks, not victories. Keeping every update in one doc for the raise.

entries.title: Sleep is the roadmap
entries.body: Two quarters of 5-hour nights and my decisions got stupid. Sleep tracking, no Slack after nine, naps allowed. The roadmap got better when I did.

entries.title: Enterprise curiosity
entries.body: Three enterprise pilots asked for SSO and audit logs. Different product gravity. Piloting one, saying no twice — focus is the strategy this year.

entries.title: Seed extension closed
entries.body: Extended the seed: 18 more months of runway without a priced round. Terms clean, board unchanged. The best fundraising is the kind you can decline.

entries.title: The pivot conversation
entries.body: June and I finally said it out loud: previews are a feature, not the company. The wedge is release confidence. Six weeks to validate or wind down gracefully.

entries.title: Kill criteria, written early
entries.body: Every bet now ships with kill criteria and a date. The pivot took six weeks instead of six months because past-us had written the exit down.

entries.title: Release confidence sells
entries.body: The pivot validated: teams pay to know a release is safe, not to see it sooner. Positioning, pricing, and roadmap all simplified in one move.

entries.title: Mentoring junior founders
entries.body: Office hours at the accelerator, two Fridays a month. Teaching runway math and kill criteria. Sam was right: context is generosity.

entries.title: Learned to sell
entries.body: Fifty sales calls this year. Engineers underestimate how learnable this is: listen, recap, ask what happens if nothing changes. The recap is the close.

entries.title: Acquisition interest memo
entries.body: Two acquirers circling. Memo for the board: what we'd need (team intact, product alive, 3-year horizon) and what we'll decline. Written before any term sheet arrives.

entries.title: Year of depth
entries.body: No new initiatives in 2026. Deepen the wedge, grow the team to nine, protect the Friday note. Boring is the strategy now.

entries.title: Seven years in
entries.body: Read my 2019 journal tonight. The kid who loved fires now writes kill criteria and sleeps eight hours. Both versions built this. Keeping both in view.
